packages.label_en: The Great Tzaddik and Song of Songs — Concealed Holiness
packages.reason: The entire Torah is built on a single bechina: the Tzaddik Gadol who conceals himself is the same essential phenomenon as Shir HaShirim, which is Kodesh Kadashim yet contains no explicit words of holiness or purity. Both share the identical nature — supreme, transcendent holiness that is precisely because of its intensity invisible to ordinary perception. The world cannot bear the Tzaddik's holiness, so he appears ordinary; readers cannot 'see' holiness in Shir HaShirim, so no holiness-words appear. The concealment (העלם) is not a deficiency but the signature of the highest degree of holiness (קדש קדשים). These three concepts — the Tzaddik, Shir HaShirim, and the state of concealed holiness — form a single thematic family united by the principle: extreme holiness effaces its own outward markers.
packages.source_quote: וְזֶה בְּחִינוֹת: כָּל הַשִּׁירִים קֹדֶשׁ, וְשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים — וְזֶה מֵחֲמַת גֹּדֶל עֹצֶם קְדֻשָּׁתוֹ אֵינָם רוֹאִים שָׁם שׁוּם קְדֻשָּׁה
